sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a house inside the City of Sarasota?
sections.html:
Sarasota County bills it. The City of Sarasota is a taxing authority that levies its own rate, but the Sarasota County Tax Collector prints one combined bill and the Sarasota County Property Appraiser sets the value that every taxing body uses.

A city address therefore means one parcel, one appraisal and one bill that carries several lines: the city, the county, the school board and special districts, plus non-ad valorem charges such as fire protection and solid waste. Look up your parcel on the appraiser's property search, then check the bill on the tax collector's site.

If you plan to sell a Sarasota house with tax due, the county offices are the ones to call. Our county property tax guide carries the full calendar, and our Sarasota selling page covers the sale itself.

sections.h2: What does the City of Sarasota say about Amendment 3?
sections.html:
The city's property tax page prints the ballot summary for Amendment 3. It says the amendment raises the homestead exemption for non-school taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, adjusted for inflation after that, and lowers the cap on non-homestead assessment increases from 10 percent to 5 percent.

The summary also says people who are not Florida residents on December 31, 2026 receive the existing exemption first, with the larger one beginning in the fifth year of exemption. It requires counties and municipalities to use property taxes only for listed purposes such as public safety, schools, infrastructure and debt service, and it takes effect January 1, 2027.

The Sarasota County Tax Collector adds that the 2026 bill must be paid as issued and that the voter-approved changes reach the bill for 2027. School Board taxes and non-ad valorem assessments stay on the notice. Ask the Property Appraiser how the change affects your parcel before you price a house for sale.

sections.h2: How does homestead work for a Sarasota city homeowner?
sections.html:
You qualify by being a Florida resident who owns and lives in the home as a permanent residence on January 1, and you apply by March 1. The county appraiser accepts later applications but treats March 1 as the timely date.

The appraiser's list of proof is long. Married couples give information for both spouses. You show ownership with a recorded deed, a tax bill or a TRIM notice, and residence with a Florida driver license or ID showing the home address. Add one more document such as voter registration or a vehicle registration, or two from a list that includes a W-2, school records, a tax return or a utility bill. If you moved from another Florida house you still own, bring proof that the old exemption was cancelled.

  • Every applicant must supply a Social Security number, as s. 196.011(1)(b) requires.
  • A permanent resident alien shows a green card.
  • Renting the house or leaving it as a non-primary home ends homestead.

sections.h2: What does Save Our Homes mean for a Sarasota seller?
sections.html:
The cap ends when you sell. After the first year of homestead, Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and a sale resets the next owner's assessed value to just value on the following January 1.

The Department of Revenue's cap chart, revised January 2026, shows a 2024 cap of 3.0 percent, a 2025 cap of 2.9 percent and a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent. Long-time owners of a Sarasota home may carry a wide gap between assessed and market value, so the buyer's first bill can be far higher than yours.

Portability lets you move part of that benefit. You must set up the new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, and file Form DR-501T with the DR-501 by March 1. Statute text caps the transfer at the lesser of $500,000 or the difference between just and assessed value of the old home, and the statute page says 2026 amendments first apply to the 2027 roll.

sections.h2: Which Sarasota exemptions are not tied to age or income?
sections.html:
Several $5,000 exemptions apply to one Florida property a permanent resident owns, and residence there is not required. The appraiser lists widow or widower, total and permanent disability, blindness, and disabled veteran at 10 percent or more.

The senior exemption is different. The appraiser's calendar says the additional senior exemption needs income documents by June 1, and a limited-income senior must be 65 or older. Veterans with a total and permanent service-connected disability can receive a full exemption on homestead, and the benefit can carry to a surviving spouse in some cases.

sections.h2: What if you owe back tax on a Sarasota house you want to sell?
sections.html:
Pay the balance from closing proceeds, or ask the tax collector how a payment will be applied. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and the collector warns that nonpayment can cost you the property.

The tax collector says the buyer must pay the entire bill whenever the purchase falls, and that the seller usually credits the buyer on the closing statement for the months of ownership. The seller does not pay the tax collector directly as a partial payment. If a bill arrives for a house you no longer own, forward it to the new owner or return it to the collector.

Another sale-time cost is the deed tax: $0.70 per $100 of consideration, rounded up to the next $100, on the clerk's fee page. Our tax deed page explains what follows a long delinquency.

sections.h2: Where can a Sarasota owner dispute a tax figure?
sections.html:
Start with the Sarasota County Property Appraiser, then use the Value Adjustment Board. The petition is due 25 days after the TRIM notice mailing, and the 2026 notices went out on August 17.

The board covers value, classification and exemptions. If your complaint is that the city millage is too high, take it to the city's budget hearings listed on the TRIM notice. Florida's calendar has taxing authorities hold hearings on tentative budgets in September and October and on final budgets after that.

sections.h2: What is a sensible order of steps for a Sarasota owner with a tax problem?
sections.html:
Work from the office that owns each question. The county appraiser owns value and exemptions, the tax collector owns the bill, and the clerk owns recorded documents.

  • Pull your parcel on the appraiser's property search and read the 2026 TRIM supplement if you have a question about a line item.
  • Confirm that your exemptions are still on the parcel after any change of name or address.
  • Check the tax collector's account page for any prior-year balance before listing the house.
  • Search the clerk's Official Records for liens that a title agent will find.
  • Register for the clerk's fraud alerts so a forged deed is reported to you by email.

The appraiser's news page says the 2026 TRIM notices could be viewed as a PDF from the parcel record by using the 2026 TRIM button near the top of the page.

faqs.q: Does the City of Sarasota collect its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. The county tax collector bills and collects, and the city is one of the taxing authorities on the combined bill. Ask the Sarasota County Tax Collector for your bill.

faqs.q: What is the Sarasota city millage rate?
faqs.a: Check your TRIM notice or the City of Sarasota's budget pages, because the rate belongs to the city and is only one part of your total. Ask the city or the Property Appraiser for the current figure.

faqs.q: When do I apply for homestead in Sarasota?
faqs.a: Apply by March 1 of the year you want the exemption, and be a resident living in the home on January 1. The appraiser may still review a late application.

faqs.q: Does Save Our Homes pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets the assessed value to just value the next January 1. You may be able to port part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead if you move within three years.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sarasota house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is normally paid out of the sale proceeds at closing, and the closing agent confirms the amount with the tax collector.
